newsitem.title: USA: Workers OK new pact at GM Ohio truck plant.
newsitem.headline: Workers OK new pact at GM Ohio truck plant.

text.p: Workers at General Motors Corp.'s Moraine, Ohio, truck plant overwhelmingly approved a new local labour contract Saturday, a week after they rejected a previous offer and went on strike, union officials said
A spokesman for Local 801 of the International Union of Electronics Workers said the revised contract was approved by a vote of 2,408 to 888.

Local 801's 4,100 members struck the plant near Dayton, Ohio, last Sunday, after workers rejected a proposed contract that included stiff penalties for absences. The absence policy was excluded from the pact approved in voting Thursday and Friday.
The walkout halted production of Chevrolet Blazer, GMC Jimmy and Oldsmobile Bravada sport/utility vehicles for two full days, costign GM about 2,000 vehicles.

In the new pact, GM agreed to hire about 64 new workers, pay a $1,000 signing bonus, pay a total of $300,000 in penalties to settle grievances and grant higher shift premium pay to the plant's third work crew.
Another auto industry labour dispute continued Saturday at two Johnson Controls Inc. truck seat plants in Michigan and Ohio -- strikes that were also affecting Ford Motor Co. production.
Jeffrey Steiner, a Johnson Controls spokesman, said negotiations were continuing with the United Auto Workers for initial contracts at the factories in Plymouth, Mich., and Oberlin, Ohio.
Workers at the plants voted to become organised by the UAW last fall in an effort that industry observers said came with Ford's blessing.

But the strikes, which started Tuesday have prevented Johnson Controls from shipping seats to Ford plants Wayne, Mich., and Lorain, Ohio, which produce the Ford Expedition sport/utility vehicle and the Econoline van.
Ford said Tuesday it would not accept seats made by non-union replacement workers at the plants and was continuing to build trucks without seats.
The Plymouth plant employs about 300 hourly workers and the Oberlin plant about 200.

Among other changes, UAW wants Milwaukee-based Johnson Controls to provide wage parity with other car and truck seat suppliers, such as Lear Corp., which pays hourly wages of $14 to $16. Wages at the Johnson Controls plants start at about $9 an hour.
